name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,433

clue.text: It makes progress difficult for a worker taking one seal off

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cap a well or pipe is to seal it off

explanation.surface: A labourer slows down by removing a seal, perhaps from a jar or document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just strings the pieces together: the worker takes one, then the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is any burden or disadvantage that hinders someone's advance, literally so in golf or horse racing.

clue.text: Time to enclose earliest of graves in large piece of granite perhaps

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
to enclose something is to put it inside, so the first word wraps round what follows
one thing in another sits inside it, so the single letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sculptor is told to take time setting a tombstone letter into a big granite block.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the grave's letter goes into the word for large first, and the time word then wraps round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the crushed stone or gravel used in building, and granite is one common example of such material.

clue.text: Put off by film featuring bloody revolutionary? Just the opposite

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the colour word is read backwards
a film featuring something holds it within; the twist that follows swaps which part holds which
this phrase swaps the roles just described, so the outer and inner parts trade places

blocks.note: bloody things are red; read backwards it becomes DER

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged by a movie starring a gory rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface instruction is undone by its last phrase: the film does not hold the revolutionary, the revolutionary holds the film.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or dissuade them, which is what putting them off means.

clue.text: Decide against keeping individual eastern dish

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the first word wraps round the next two

blocks.note: to cast aside or out is to reject, which is deciding against something
a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul'

explanation.surface: Someone rejects the idea of holding on to a single oriental meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern' looks like part of the definition but only supplies E; the dish is French, not Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked French stew of beans with sausage and duck or pork, a classic regional dish.

clue.text: Defend positive method of learning at court

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for positive
learning by rote is memorising through repetition
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A lawyer defends their client with a confident, well-rehearsed approach in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect is to guard or shield from harm, the same as defending against attack.

clue.text: Consternation shown by Tory leader after party, falling short, goes west

indicators.note: falling short means not reaching the end, so the word loses its final letter
in an across clue, going west means travelling right to left, so the letters run backwards
one piece placed after another simply follows it in the answer

blocks.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest; cut short and turned round it gives DIS
Theresa May, Conservative leader and Prime Minister 2016-19

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads as a Conservative leader follows a faltering party that collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory leader' tempts you to take T, its first letter; it is the whole name of a Tory leader. 'goes west' also suggests dying, but here it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is the sudden distress and alarm felt at something unexpected, a close synonym of consternation.

clue.text: Doctor having trouble with training exercise

blocks.note: ill as a noun is trouble or misfortune

explanation.surface: A physician struggles during a workout routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated routine used to train soldiers or teams, so it is a kind of practice exercise.

clue.text: Second trial involves girl stabbed by head of French firm

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken
to involve is to wrap up within, so the trial surrounds what follows
something stabbed has a blade pushed into it, so the letter goes inside the girl's name

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A second court hearing involves a young woman knifed by a French company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' is not a company but the adjective meaning unwavering. The French letter goes into the girl first, and that pair then sits inside the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolutely unwavering, and firm is used in exactly that sense of someone who will not budge.

clue.text: Tolerate an element of Pan-Arab ideology

indicators.note: an element is a component part, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to put up with one strand of a political creed uniting the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something, usually in the negative 'can't abide', is to bear or put up with it.

clue.text: Playing sage at marbles

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A wise old man is enjoying a game of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marbles' reads as the game being played but is the definition: agates are a type of glass or stone marble.
explanation.definitionFit: Agates were the prized banded-stone marbles of children's games, and the name stuck for glass shooters too.

clue.text: Inflamed swelling originally overlooked by girl when dressing maybe

indicators.note: the original letter is left out, so the word loses its first letter
one thing by another sits next to it, so the pieces join side by side

blocks.note: a boil is an inflamed swelling on the skin; minus its first letter it leaves OIL

explanation.surface: A girl ignores a sore lump when bandaging a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers 'dressing' towards bandages and wounds; it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a common salad dressing on its own or the base of a vinaigrette, hence 'maybe' for an example.

clue.text: Useless welder left one by mistake

indicators.note: letters set down by mistake end up in the wrong order and need rearranging

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hopeless welder abandoned a piece through an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is a feckless good-for-nothing, and the term is also used adjectivally for someone idle and worthless.

clue.text: Went running back when late

indicators.note: running back means heading the opposite way, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted back once they realised they were behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went running' looks like one phrase; 'Went' is the word that gets turned round, and 'running back' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean far advanced in time, as in 'deep into the night', which is how late is meant.

clue.text: Discontinue with article on church in the middle of Vaucluse

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central part, here the two centre letters
in an across clue one word on another sits right after it
one thing in another sits within it, so the joined words go inside the selected letters

blocks.note: the central two letters of this eight-letter French department

explanation.surface: A grammar point about churches in Provence: one region's services are called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel something is to call it off or stop it, the same as to discontinue it.

clue.text: Temporary alliance getting into trouble after Conservative leader starts to oppose all liberal initiatives

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the starts of the following words are their first letters
a word in trouble is in a mess, so its letters are disordered
one piece after another simply follows it

blocks.note: first letters of these four words
the letters to rearrange, giving TION

explanation.surface: A political pact runs into difficulties as the Tory chief resists every Liberal policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'into' is the anagram fodder, and 'initiatives' is not a signal but the fourth word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is a pact between parties to govern together, typically lasting only until an election or crisis ends it.

clue.text: Still taken aback over separate political movement

indicators.note: taken aback, read literally, is taken backwards, so the word runs right to left
one thing over another covers it, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: still in the sense of 'even now'

explanation.surface: Someone is still shocked by a breakaway faction in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' sounds like surprise but is a reversal instruction, and 'Still' is not an adjective but means yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party was the US right-wing populist movement that rose around 2009, named after the Boston protest.

clue.text: Old actress hiding drugs after first of arrests in Nice

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone
to hide something is to hold it inside, so the actress's name goes around the drugs
in a down clue, after means placed below, so the single letter comes first

blocks.note: Betty Grable, Hollywood star of the 1940s
E is ecstasy, so drugs in the plural is two of them

explanation.surface: A veteran film star is caught concealing narcotics after police arrests on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city, matching the arrests scene; it is the adjective meaning pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable describes something pleasant or likeable, which is what nice means as an adjective.

clue.text: It provides protection for exotic air plant seen around Utah primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the state name gives only its first letter
something exotic is strange and outlandish, so the letters take an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A tropical air plant growing in the American West shelters some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'air plant' are placed around U, which joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet stretched over goods or equipment to shield them from the weather.

clue.text: Bottle shown by philosopher reportedly trapped by wild animal

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the name is replaced by a word that sounds the same
something trapped is held inside, so the animal's word wraps round the sound-alike

explanation.surface: A wine bottle is said to show a thinker caught by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' could be the verb or slang for courage; here it is simply a glass vessel for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass vessel into which wine or spirits are poured for serving, a type of bottle.

clue.text: Russia's principal author coming around to accept island's mysterious quality

indicators.note: the principal letter is the chief, first one
coming around means turning about, so the author's name runs backwards
to accept something is to take it in, so the name holds the island

explanation.surface: A leading Russian writer comes round to embracing an island's enigmatic charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia's principal author' suggests Tolstoy or Pushkin, but 'principal' takes only Russia's first letter and the author is Eco.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance can mean an aura of glamour, mystery and remoteness, as in 'the romance of the desert'.

clue.text: Delay caused by extremely efficient soldiers returning to block road

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters
returning means going back the way they came, so the letters run backwards
something that blocks a road sits within it, so these letters go inside the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Hold-ups caused by a crack military unit that turns back and closes a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to slow or hold up its progress, the verb sense of delay.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff on independent film-maker

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another is simply joined to it

blocks.note: tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Cheap junk appears in an indie director's film.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was the French director and star of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati wrote, directed and starred in French comedies such as Playtime and Mon Oncle.

clue.text: Modify point in support of Australian lawyer

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
a district attorney, the US public prosecutor
PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Someone changes a legal argument to back up an Aussie barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter or adjust it for a new purpose, which is a kind of modification.

clue.text: Intended to make a profit from organised crime after a short time back in California

indicators.note: going back reverses direction, so the short word is read right to left
organised means put in order, so the letters are arranged afresh
one piece after another follows it in the answer
one thing in another sits inside it, so the state's abbreviation surrounds the rest

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, giving MERCI

explanation.surface: A West Coast racket built for money: gangsters set up after a brief return to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised crime' reads as the Mafia, but 'organised' is the anagram signal and 'crime' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercial describes a venture run for financial gain rather than as a hobby or charity.

clue.text: Communist academic revealing its use may be divisive

explanation.surface: A Marxist professor shows that their influence splits opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divisive' in the surface is political; in the definition it means literally dividing parts of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma separates clauses and items in a list, so its job is literally to divide a sentence up.

clue.text: Competes fiercely after commencement of game

indicators.note: taking only what comes after the start drops the opening letter

blocks.note: to scrap is to fight; the opening S is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Players battle hard once a match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commencement of game' looks like taking G; instead 'after commencement of' says start after the first letter of SCRAPS, leaving CRAPS, and 'game' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Craps is a dice game for gambling, popular in American casinos and street play.

clue.text: The initial piece captures old boxer's charm

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter
a piece that captures something takes it in, so the boxer's name goes inside

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, with the possessive S
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A chess opening sees one piece take a former boxer's lucky amulet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The initial piece' is read as one unit, the T plus the chess piece, so the boxer lands between those two parts rather than inside the piece alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck or ward off harm, the same as a lucky charm.

clue.text: Dog licence finally found in suitcase with a couple of letters

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it
something found in a case is inside it, so the letter goes within
a couple is two, so only the first two letters of the next word are taken

blocks.note: the first two letters of letters

explanation.surface: A pet's licence turns up in luggage along with some correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound with floppy ears, bred for hunting hares, so it is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Verse from South Africa on resistance mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
one piece on another is joined to it in sequence

blocks.note: to make a stand is to resist; trimmed it gives STAN
ZA is South Africa's international code

explanation.surface: A poem from South Africa that is largely about the struggle against apartheid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South' tempts you to take S; the whole of 'South Africa' is ZA, from the Afrikaans Zuid-Afrika.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, and verse can mean exactly such a unit.

clue.text: A service flat that will do on the outskirts of Nuremberg

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: 'so' as in 'so be it', accepting enough
first and last letters of Nuremberg

explanation.surface: An apartment that will suffice on the edge of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is a home in the surface but an adjective in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in cathedrals and churches around sunset.
